notes.front: What is a colony, in one sentence?
notes.back: A settlement ruled by a European country; England created 13 colonies in North America.
notes.explanation: Every later event in this topic (slavery, taxation, revolution) happens inside these 13 colonies.
notes.example: Jamestown, England's first permanent colony, founded in 1607.

notes.front: What was the Colonial Period, in one sentence?
notes.back: The era starting in 1607, when England founded its first permanent settlement, Jamestown, and lasting until independence.
notes.explanation: It is the time when England ruled the 13 colonies.
notes.example: England created 13 colonies across this period.

notes.front: Who are American Indians, in one sentence?
notes.back: The people who lived in the Americas before Europeans arrived; also called Native Americans.
notes.explanation: Different tribes had their own cultures, languages and forms of government long before 1607.
notes.example: Tribes living across North America for thousands of years before Jamestown.

notes.front: What is an enslaved person, in one sentence?
notes.back: Someone forced to work with no freedom; millions of enslaved Africans were taken to the Americas and sold.
notes.explanation: Enslaved Africans were forced to work on farms in terrible conditions.
notes.example: A person bought and sold, forced to work on a tobacco or cotton farm.

notes.front: What is taxation without representation, in one sentence?
notes.back: Britain raised colonists' taxes without letting their representatives vote on the new taxes.
notes.explanation: It became a major colonial grievance and a reason given for declaring independence.
notes.example: A new British tax on tea, imposed with no colonial vote in Parliament.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: What was the American Revolution, in one sentence?
notes.back: The war, 1775 to 1783, in which the colonies won independence from Great Britain.
notes.explanation: It began because the colonists lacked self-government and objected to British taxes.
notes.example: Also called the Revolutionary War, or the War for Independence.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: What was the Continental Army, in one sentence?
notes.back: The colonists' army during the American Revolution; George Washington was its general.
notes.explanation: It is one reason Washington is called the "Father of Our Country."
notes.example: Example: Washington's soldiers spent the winter of 1777 at Valley Forge.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: What was the Battle of Yorktown, in one sentence?
notes.back: Where the British Army surrendered in 1781, ending the fighting of the American Revolution.
notes.explanation: A peace treaty confirming US independence followed two years later, in 1783.
notes.example: Fought in Virginia; the British commander surrendered his army there.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: What are the 13 original states, in one sentence?
notes.back: The 13 colonies became the 13 original states when the Declaration of Independence was adopted.
notes.explanation: They are the founding members of the United States, before any other state joined.
notes.example: New Hampshire and Georgia were both among the 13, at opposite ends of the coast.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: Who was Thomas Jefferson, in one sentence?
notes.back: The writer of the Declaration of Independence, and later the third President of the United States.
notes.explanation: His name is closely tied to the Declaration's ideas of natural rights and self-government.
notes.example: He wrote that people have the right to "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness."
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: Who was George Washington, in one sentence?
notes.back: General of the Continental Army in the Revolution and the first President, 1789 to 1797.
notes.explanation: He is called the "Father of Our Country" for leading both the army and the new government.
notes.example: He presided over the Constitutional Convention before becoming President.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 9 "A New Government and an Expanding Nation"

notes.front: Who was Benjamin Franklin, in one sentence?
notes.back: A Founder famous as the diplomat who negotiated the 1783 peace treaty with Britain.
notes.explanation: He was also the first Postmaster General of the United States.
notes.example: He also started the first free public libraries.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: Who was James Madison, in one sentence?
notes.back: Called the "Father of the Constitution"; the fourth President and a writer of the Federalist Papers.
notes.explanation: He helped draft the Constitution and then helped explain and defend it to the public.
notes.example: He later served as President during the War of 1812.

notes.front: Who was Alexander Hamilton, in one sentence?
notes.back: The first Secretary of the Treasury and one of the writers of the Federalist Papers.
notes.explanation: He helped establish the First Bank of the United States as part of setting up federal finances.
notes.example: He had earlier served as an aide to General George Washington.

notes.front: Who was John Jay, in one sentence?
notes.back: One of the three writers of the Federalist Papers, alongside Madison and Hamilton.
notes.explanation: He is the least famous of the three, but the papers are still credited to all three.
notes.example: He later became the first Chief Justice of the United States (supremecourt.gov).
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 9 "A New Government and an Expanding Nation"

notes.front: What was Publius, in one sentence?
notes.back: The name Madison, Hamilton and Jay all signed on the Federalist Papers, instead of their own names.
notes.explanation: All of the writers of the Federalist Papers signed the essays with the name "Publius."
notes.example: All 85 essays carry the same signature, "Publius," though three different men wrote them.

notes.front: The colonists came to America for many reasons. Name one?
notes.explanation: Many people came for freedom, for example to practice their religion. Other accepted answers: political liberty; religious freedom; economic opportunity; escape persecution.

notes.front: Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
notes.explanation: They had lived in the Americas for thousands of years before 1607. Other accepted answer: Native Americans. (65/20)

notes.front: What group of people was taken and sold as slaves?
notes.explanation: Millions of enslaved Africans were forced onto ships and taken to North and South America. Other accepted answer: people from Africa.

notes.front: What war did the Americans fight to win independence from Britain?
notes.explanation: It ran 1775 to 1783. Other accepted answers: the (American) Revolutionary War; War for (American) Independence.

notes.front: Name one reason why the Americans declared independence from Britain?
notes.explanation: Many colonists said it was not fair to pay taxes when they had no vote. Other accepted answers: taxation without representation; British soldiers stayed in Americans' houses (boarding, quartering); they did not have self-government; Boston Massacre; Boston Tea Party (Tea Act); Stamp Act; Sugar Act; Townshend Acts; Intolerable (Coercive) Acts.

notes.front: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
notes.explanation: Jefferson wrote the statement that announced American independence. (65/20)

notes.front: When was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
notes.explanation: This is why the United States celebrates Independence Day on July 4 every year.

notes.front: The American Revolution had many important events. Name one?
notes.explanation: The Revolution included several named battles and turning points. Other accepted answers: Declaration of Independence; Washington Crossing the Delaware (Battle of Trenton); (Battle of) Saratoga; Valley Forge (Encampment); (Battle of) Yorktown (British surrender at Yorktown).

notes.front: There were 13 original states. Name five?
notes.back: New Hampshire, Massachusetts, New York, Virginia, Georgia.
notes.explanation: The 13 original states are named individually on the cards that follow. Other accepted answers: Rhode Island; Connecticut; New Jersey; Pennsylvania; Delaware; Maryland; North Carolina; South Carolina.

notes.front: Is New Hampshire one of the 13 original states (question 81)?
notes.explanation: It is one of the 13 colonies that became the 13 original states in 1776.

notes.front: Is Massachusetts one of the 13 original states (question 81)?
notes.explanation: It is one of the 13 colonies that became the 13 original states in 1776.

notes.explanation: It is one of the 13 colonies that became the 13 original states in 1776.

notes.explanation: It is one of the 13 colonies that became the 13 original states in 1776.

notes.front: Is South Carolina one of the 13 original states (question 81)?
notes.explanation: It is one of the 13 colonies that became the 13 original states in 1776.

notes.front: Is Georgia one of the 13 original states (question 81)?
notes.explanation: It is one of the 13 colonies that became the 13 original states in 1776.

notes.front: Is Vermont one of the 13 original states (question 81)?
notes.explanation: Vermont was an independent republic in 1776 and did not join the United States as a state until 1791, after the 13 original states.

notes.front: Is Maine one of the 13 original states (question 81)?
notes.explanation: Maine was part of Massachusetts in 1776 and did not become its own state until 1820, after the 13 original states.

notes.front: What founding document was written in 1787?
notes.explanation: It was written 11 years after the Declaration of Independence.

notes.front: The Federalist Papers supported the passage of the U.S. Constitution. Name one of the writers?
notes.explanation: Three men wrote the Federalist Papers, all signed "Publius." Other accepted answers: (Alexander) Hamilton; (John) Jay; Publius.

notes.front: Why were the Federalist Papers important?
notes.back: They helped people understand the (U.S.) Constitution.
notes.explanation: The essays explained the new Constitution to the public to win support for it. Other accepted answer: they supported passing the (U.S.) Constitution.

notes.front: Benjamin Franklin is famous for many things. Name one?
notes.back: Founded the first free public libraries.
notes.explanation: He started libraries anyone could use for free. Other accepted answers: first Postmaster General of the United States; helped write the Declaration of Independence; inventor; U.S. diplomat.

notes.front: George Washington is famous for many things. Name one?
notes.explanation: Washington led the army and then the new government. One of the 20 questions for 65/20 applicants. (65/20) Other accepted answers: first president of the United States; general of the Continental Army; President of the Constitutional Convention.

notes.front: Thomas Jefferson is famous for many things. Name one?
notes.back: Writer of the Declaration of Independence.
notes.explanation: He wrote the words "all men are created equal." Other accepted answers: third president of the United States; doubled the size of the United States (Louisiana Purchase); first Secretary of State; founded the University of Virginia; writer of the Virginia Statute on Religious Freedom.

notes.front: James Madison is famous for many things. Name one?
notes.explanation: He planned much of the Constitution. Other accepted answers: fourth president of the United States; President during the War of 1812; one of the writers of the Federalist Papers.

notes.front: Alexander Hamilton is famous for many things. Name one?
notes.explanation: He set up the new country's money system. Other accepted answers: one of the writers of the Federalist Papers; helped establish the First Bank of the United States; aide to General George Washington; member of the Continental Congress.

notes.front: The American Revolutionary War ran from {{c1::1775 to 1783}}.
notes.explanation: Fighting stopped after Yorktown in 1781, but the war did not officially end until the 1783 treaty.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: In what year did the British Army surrender at the Battle of Yorktown?
notes.explanation: Fighting ended there, though the formal peace treaty was not signed until 1783.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: A 1600s settlement in North America is governed under England's rule, not on its own. What is this called?
notes.explanation: England eventually created 13 such settlements along the Atlantic coast.

notes.front: Before 1607, millions of people already lived across North and South America. What are they called?
notes.explanation: They lived there long before any European colony was founded.

notes.front: A person is forced to work on a Virginia tobacco farm with no freedom and no pay. What is this called?
notes.explanation: Millions of Africans were forced into this condition in the American colonies.

notes.front: Britain raises the colonists' taxes but lets no colonial representative vote on the new law. What is this called?
notes.explanation: It became one of the colonists' central complaints against British rule.
notes.choices:
A) Taxation without representation
B) A poll tax
C) A tariff
notes.choicesExplained: B is wrong: a poll tax is a fee to vote, unrelated to colonial-era Parliament. C is wrong: a tariff is a specific kind of tax on imports, not the general grievance described.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: In 1775, the 13 colonies go to war with Britain to win independence. What is this war called?
notes.explanation: It lasted until 1783, when Britain formally recognised US independence.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: When the Declaration of Independence was adopted, what did the 13 colonies become?
notes.explanation: Adopting the Declaration turned colonies into states of a new country.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: Who wrote the document announcing American independence in 1776?
notes.explanation: He later became the third President.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: Who led the colonial army during the Revolution and later became the first President?
notes.explanation: He is called the "Father of Our Country" for both roles.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 9 "A New Government and an Expanding Nation"

notes.front: Which Founder travelled abroad as a diplomat and negotiated the 1783 peace treaty with Britain?
notes.explanation: He was also the first Postmaster General of the United States.
notes.source: Study guide (M-1175), Chapter 8 "The American Revolutionary War & the Declaration of Independence"

notes.front: Which Federalist Papers writer is also called the "Father of the Constitution"?
notes.explanation: He both helped draft the Constitution and helped defend it in the Federalist Papers.

notes.front: Which Federalist Papers writer became the first Secretary of the Treasury?
notes.explanation: He set up the federal government's early finances, including the First Bank of the United States.
